Method of Attack: Scammers trick users into calling a fake billing notice phone number, then guide them to download remote access software (AnyDesk, TeamViewer) to gain unattended access to the victim's computer.
Use of fake antivirus billing renewal emails pretending to be from Norton Lifelock, Microsoft, and McAfee to lure victims.
Installation of fake malware scanners (batch script mimicking SonicWall scanner) to scare victims.
Collection of personal information under the pretense of processing refunds.
Use of remote access to install malware or enlist devices into spam botnets.
Attack Vector: Phishing emails with fake billing notices containing phone numbers to call.
Social engineering via phone calls to convince victims to install remote access software.
Fake support websites (e.g., 1800support.weebly.com mimicking BestBuy Geek Squad).
Indicators of Compromise: Emails pretending to be billing notices from Norton Lifelock, Microsoft, McAfee charging $350-$399 for 3-year subscriptions.
Phone number included in emails to call for subscription cancellation.
Fake 'Sonicwall Approved by the NSA' scanner batch file using wevtutil.exe to clear Windows event logs.
